newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo says good prospects for IMF membership - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugo says good prospects for IMF membership - paper.

text.p: Yugoslav Finance Minister Tomica Raicevic said there were good prospects for Yugoslavia normalizing its membership in the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Belgrade papers reported on Friday.

"I feel we can say the talks are being held in a favourable atmosphere and there are real prospects for our status in the fund to be normalized. In any case things are moving in a good direction," Raicevic said.

Raicevic was speaking in Washington where he headed a Yugoslav government delegation in two-day talks with IMF officials, initiated by Belgrade, on restoring rump Yugoslavia's membership with the organisation.
The talks, initiated by Belgrade, ended on Thursday.
The Yugoslav delegation submitted to the IMF legal documents expressing the government's and parliament's resolve to meet all statutory obligations stemming from membership in the organization.
Last week the Yugoslav parliament endorsed what the government described as all conditions set by the IMF to restore Belgrade's membership.

IMF membership is a crucial step in Belgrade's efforts to bring in foreign capital to repair its economy, devastated by three and a half years of international sanctions imposed due to its role in the war in Bosnia.
